name: targets-starter
about: A starter account sees only the tiers it may use (sealed or stronger here), and starter says so: isolation at that tier or stronger, never an open network (an open network asked for gets the starter allow list).

benefits: A separate kernel in user space (gVisor): the host kernel's attack surface is cut
Fastest cold start of SandHold's engines (about <span>); warm about <span>
limits: Open network on this node: no allow list is enforced here
Some system calls are unsupported or slower (heavy file and network I/O)
about.title: SandHold Sealed

targets.name: gvisor
targets.tierMeans: its own kernel in user space

benefits: Its own guest kernel in a hardware-virtualised VM (Kata Containers): the strongest separation
Warm start about <span> from the node's pool
limits: Open network on this node: no allow list is enforced here
about.title: SandHold Vault

targets.name: kata
targets.tierMeans: its own kernel in a virtual machine

tiers.bestFor: Code you or your team wrote: quick scripts and checks, where starting in milliseconds matters most
tiers.means: a jailed process on the host's kernel
tiers.title: Shared
tiers.tradeOff: Shares the host's kernel: a flaw in that kernel reaches the host

tiers.bestFor: Code an AI wrote, or code nobody has reviewed: tests and builds that need a full image
tiers.means: a hardened container on the host's kernel
tiers.title: Shielded
tiers.tradeOff: Still on the host's kernel, behind the container's filters

tiers.bestFor: Code from a stranger, or code that may be hostile: a bug in the host's kernel is out of its reach
tiers.means: its own kernel in user space
tiers.title: Sealed
tiers.tradeOff: Some system calls are slower or unsupported

tiers.bestFor: Hostile code that also needs the open internet, or work that must stay furthest from the host and from other sandboxes
tiers.means: its own kernel in a virtual machine
tiers.title: Vault
tiers.tradeOff: The slowest cold start, and more memory per sandbox
